why: New behavioral node corpus/spec-floor — the harness that runs the project-spec-tier engines across the corpus, specified for the first time (the engine shipped ungoverned by any node). 22 boolean scenarios over four groups. Cold sdd-spec-judge ALIGNED true, oracle/builder/architect all PASS on round 5, after four rounds that each found real defects and were each fixed at the rule rather than the instance: a governance pre-flight block that was a genuine omission of five bars, two Given-format violations, an unargued near-duplicate, one regression of the mission's own round-2 remediation (a decision carried in scenario-map prose instead of drawn in the CFG) that was re-planned rather than patched again, and a dead edge where only one of the coverage guard's two conditions was exercised. The re-plan also corrected an ordering error the graph had carried since the first draft, resolving the repo root above a directory it had not yet determined. ADDITIVE: no standing scenario in any suite narrowed, rewritten or deleted, so every @frozen file self-clears untouched and no Clearance is owed. The destructive edit is at the CLI surface rather than the contract — the removal of --check-coverage from a bin-exposed script, minor at 0.2.x, declared breaking in the changeset and argued as the point of the CR rather than a side effect. Both of issue #5's triggers reproduced against main before the fix and fail the root chain after it. Grill ran past the default three-round cap; continued on a stated convergence trend rather than auto-accepting, and the overrun was reported to the owner rather than absorbed silently.

Cold sdd-impl-judge IMPLEMENTATION_PASS true, BLOCKER null, all 22 frozen scenarios re-derived independently rather than read off the producer's assertions — where the producer asserted only an exit code the judge built its own fixtures and ran the real CLI over both streams. Both of issue #5's triggers verified empirically: a node truncated mid-file and a node whose README and frozen suite were removed each exit non-zero on the corpus scope here, and by direct reading of origin/main's main() would have exited 0 there. The judge confirmed check-spec-state — carrying the impl gate's own guards against implemented-without-a-recorded-ratification and implemented-without-a-durable-ledger-line — now runs from the root chain once per swept project-spec, where it had been unreachable from CI. Structural read clean: the loops.md anchor repair ruled a genuine blocking precondition rather than smuggled scope, the minor-at-0.2.x semver class ruled correct for a breaking bin-exposed flag removal, docs accurate against runtime output, no absorption findings, sound verification pyramid. The judge's own mutation sweep found four verification gaps and no implementation defect; all four were closed before this gate wrote. Verdict was rendered on the four-commit tree; the fifth commit is additive verification plus the produced-by map, and git diff confirms the implementation and the frozen .feature are byte-identical between the graded tree and HEAD. One process correction recorded against this mission: the conductor edited the worktree while the judge was grading it, which the judge correctly reported as an unexplained concurrent modification.
